data.title: Protonated Titanates and TiO2 Nanostructured Materials: Synthesis, Properties, and Applications
data.authors: Dmitry V. Bavykin; J. M. Friedrich; F. C. Walsh
data.topics: TiO2 Photocatalysis and Solar Cells; Mesoporous Materials and Catalysis; Chemical and Physical Properties of Materials
data.clean_abstract: Abstract Tubular and fibrous nanostructures of titanates have recently been synthesized and characterized. Three general approaches (template assisted, anodic oxidation, and alkaline hydrothermal) for the preparation of nanostructured titanate and TiO2 are reviewed. The crystal structures, morphologies, and mechanism of formation of nanostructured titanates produced by the alkaline hydrothermal method are critically discussed. The physicochemical properties of nanostructured titanates are highlighted and the links between properties and applications are emphasized. Examples of early applications of nanostructured titanates in catalysis, photocatalysis, electrocatalysis, lithium batteries, hydrogen storage, and solar‐cell technologies are reviewed. The stability of titanate nanotubes at elevated temperatures and in acid media is considered.

data.title: Photocatalytic Carbon‐Nanotube–TiO2 Composites
data.authors: Karran V. Woan; Georgios Pyrgiotakis; Wolfgang M. Sigmund
data.topics: TiO2 Photocatalysis and Solar Cells; Advanced Photocatalysis Techniques; Advanced oxidation water treatment
data.clean_abstract: Abstract The literature and advances in photocatalysis based on the combination of titania (TiO2) and carbon nanotubes is presented. The semiconductor basis for photocatalysis is introduced for anatase and rutile. Furthermore, the proposed mechanisms of catalytic enhancement resulting from the pairing of the titania semiconductor with either metallic, semiconducting, or defect‐rich carbon nanotubes (CNT) is discussed. Differences are apparent for the mixtures and chemically bonded CNT–TiO2 composites. The article then highlights the recent advances in the synthesis techniques for these composites and their photocatalytic reactions with organic, inorganic, and biological agents. Finally, various applications and challenges for these composite materials are reported.
